authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: Prakrit *sūī*, Hindi/Bihari *sūī*, Gujarati *soy* and Marathi *sūī* are explicitly in CDIAL’s first branch. The c-loss and resulting vowel sequence support these forms, separately from *suji* or nasalised c-retaining *sūñcī*. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL lists Prakrit *loṇa/lūṇa*, Marwari *lūṇ*, Marathi *loṇ*, Maithili *non* and Bhojpuri *nūn*. Both the lateral and initial-n variants are explicitly represented; the distinct namak loan family is excluded. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL gives Gujarati *nām*, Old Marwari *nāva* and Marathi *nā̃v/nāv* beneath *nāman*. Both m and v outcomes are therefore supported; the emphatic particle *nāma* (7064) is a separate entry and is not the parent. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.
